steps.message:
I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close September 30, 2026 at 5:00 PM ET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

“ET” in late September means Eastern Time in North America, which is on daylight saving time then: **EDT (UTC−4)**.

Madrid, Spain in late September is on **CEST (UTC+2)**.

So Madrid is **6 hours ahead** of ET at that date.

- **September 30, 2026, 5:00 PM ET**
- plus 6 hours
- **October 1, 2026, 11:00**

ANSWER: 2026-10-01 23:00

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Deadline: July 15, 2026, 12:00 UTC."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Lima, Peru is on Peru Time (PET), which is UTC−5 year-round and does not observe daylight saving time.

So:

- Deadline given: 2026-07-15 12:00 UTC
- Convert UTC to Lima time: subtract 5 hours
- Result: 2026-07-15 07:00 in Lima

ANSWER: 2026-07-15 07:00

I live in Tokyo, Japan. A contest page says: "Applications are due June 1, 2026 at 9:00 AM CEST."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

CEST is Central European Summer Time, which is UTC+2.

Tokyo, Japan is JST, which is UTC+9 and does not observe daylight saving time.

So Tokyo is 7 hours ahead of CEST.

June 1, 2026 at 9:00 AM CEST + 7 hours = June 1, 2026 at 4:00 PM in Tokyo.

ANSWER: 2026-06-01 16:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The contest ends on October 11, 2026 at 11:59 PM PDT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Madrid is on CEST (UTC+2) in early October, while PDT is UTC−7.

So Madrid is 9 hours ahead of PDT.

11:59 PM PDT on October 11, 2026 + 9 hours = 8:59 AM on October 12, 2026 in Madrid.

ANSWER: 2026-10-12 08:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close March 3, 2026 at 11:59 PM PST."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

“PST” means Pacific Standard Time, which is UTC−8.

Madrid, Spain in early March is on CET, which is UTC+1 (daylight saving time has not started yet).

So Madrid is 9 hours ahead of PST. Add 9 hours to:

- March 3, 2026, 11:59 PM PST
= March 4, 2026, 8:59 AM in Madrid

ANSWER: 2026-03-04 08:59

I live in Los Angeles, USA. A contest page says: "Deadline: 10:00 AM CET, February 2, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

In early February, **CET** is **UTC+1**.  
Los Angeles in February is on **PST**, which is **UTC−8**.

So Los Angeles is **9 hours behind CET**.

**10:00 AM CET on February 2, 2026** minus 9 hours = **1:00 AM in Los Angeles on February 2, 2026**.

ANSWER: 2026-02-02 01:00

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Submit by 8:00 AM JST on May 5, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Japan Standard Time (JST) is UTC+9 and does not observe daylight saving time.

Lima, Peru is PET, which is UTC-5 and also does not observe daylight saving time.

So Lima is 14 hours behind JST.

Subtract 14 hours from **2026-05-05 08:00 JST**:
- 8:00 AM on May 5 in Japan
- minus 14 hours
- = **6:00 PM on May 4** in Lima

ANSWER: 2026-05-04 18:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close October 28, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

“PT” means Pacific Time. On October 28, 2026, Pacific Time is still on daylight saving time, so it is PDT (UTC−7). Madrid in late October 2026 is on CET (UTC+1), because Spain’s daylight saving time ends the previous weekend.

So Madrid is 8 hours ahead of Pacific Time at that moment.

11:59 PM PT on October 28, 2026 + 8 hours = 7:59 AM on October 29, 2026 in Madrid.

ANSWER: 2026-10-29 07:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The live session starts October 30, 2026, 9:00 AM ET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

“ET” in late October usually means U.S. Eastern Time, and on October 30, 2026 the eastern U.S. is still on daylight saving time, so that is **EDT (UTC−4)**. Madrid on that date is already back to **CET (UTC+1)** after Europe’s DST change.

So Madrid is **5 hours ahead** of ET.

9:00 AM ET + 5 hours = **2:00 PM** in Madrid.

ANSWER: 2026-10-30 14:00

I live in New York, USA. A contest page says: "Voting closes October 27, 2026 at 18:00 CET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

On October 27, 2026, **CET** means **Central European Time = UTC+1**.

New York on that date will still be on **EDT = UTC-4** (since U.S. daylight saving time ends later, in early November).

So New York is **5 hours behind** CET.

**18:00 CET − 5 hours = 13:00 in New York** on the same date.

ANSWER: 2026-10-27 13:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Final round closes November 2, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

“PT” in early November can be ambiguous because daylight saving time may have just ended. In 2026, the U.S. switches from Pacific Daylight Time to Pacific Standard Time on November 1, so on **November 2, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT**, that means **Pacific Standard Time (UTC−8)**.

Madrid on that date is on **CET (UTC+1)**.

So Madrid is **9 hours ahead** of Pacific Standard Time:
- 2026-11-02 23:59 PT
- plus 9 hours
- = **2026-11-03 08:59** in Madrid

ANSWER: 2026-11-03 08:59 (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close March 20, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

“PT” means Pacific Time. On March 20, 2026, that is **Pacific Daylight Time (PDT, UTC-7)** because daylight saving time in the U.S. has already started.

Madrid, Spain on March 20, 2026 is **CET (UTC+1)** because Spain’s daylight saving time starts later in March.

So Madrid is **8 hours ahead** of Pacific Time on that date.

11:59 PM PT on March 20, 2026 + 8 hours = **7:59 AM on March 21, 2026** in Madrid.

ANSWER: 2026-03-21 07:59

I live in Los Angeles, USA. A contest page says: "The webinar starts March 25, 2026, 12:00 PM CET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

On March 25, 2026, **CET** is **UTC+1**.  
Los Angeles in late March is on **PDT** (**UTC-7**), because daylight saving time has already started.

So Los Angeles is **8 hours behind** CET.

**12:00 PM CET − 8 hours = 4:00 AM in Los Angeles** on the same date.

ANSWER: 2026-03-25 04:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Deadline: 12:00 AM ET on October 12, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

“12:00 AM ET on October 12, 2026” means midnight at the very start of October 12 in Eastern Time.

On October 12, 2026:
- Eastern Time will be EDT (UTC−4), since the U.S. is still on daylight saving time.
- Madrid, Spain will be on CEST (UTC+2), since Spain is also still on daylight saving time.

Madrid is therefore 6 hours ahead of Eastern Time.

So:
- 2026-10-12 00:00 ET
- plus 6 hours
- = 2026-10-12 06:00 in Madrid

ANSWER: 2026-10-12 06:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Papers are due October 9, 2026 (23:59 AoE)."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

“AoE” means **Anywhere on Earth**, which is conventionally the time zone **UTC−12:00**.

So:

- Deadline given: **2026-10-09 23:59 AoE (UTC−12)**
- Convert to UTC: add 12 hours → **2026-10-10 11:59 UTC**

Madrid on **October 10, 2026** is on **CEST (UTC+2)**, since Spain has not yet switched back to standard time.

- Convert UTC to Madrid time: add 2 hours → **2026-10-10 13:59** in Madrid

ANSWER: 2026-10-10 13:59 (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Registration closes 12:00 PM PT, August 14, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

“PT” in August means Pacific Time observing daylight saving time, i.e. PDT (UTC−7).

Madrid in August observes CEST (UTC+2).

So Madrid is 9 hours ahead of Pacific Daylight Time:
12:00 PM PT on August 14, 2026 + 9 hours = 21:00 on August 14, 2026 in Madrid.

ANSWER: 2026-08-14 21:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Deadline: 11:59 PM IST, November 10, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

“IST” in contest pages usually means India Standard Time, which is UTC+5:30.

Madrid in November uses CET, which is UTC+1:00.

So Madrid is 4 hours 30 minutes behind India Standard Time.

11:59 PM IST on November 10, 2026  
→ subtract 4 hours 30 minutes  
→ 7:29 PM in Madrid on November 10, 2026

ANSWER: 2026-11-10 19:29

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Submissions close at 5:00 PM Nepal time on April 2, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Nepal Time is **NPT (UTC+5:45)**, and Lima, Peru is **PET (UTC-5:00)**.

So Lima is **10 hours 45 minutes behind** Nepal.

- **Deadline in Nepal:** 2026-04-02 17:00
- Subtract **10 hours 45 minutes**
- **In Lima:** 2026-04-02 06:15

ANSWER: 2026-04-02 06:15

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Applications close 10:00 AM Adelaide time, October 6, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Adelaide, South Australia is usually on Australian Central Daylight Time in early October, which is UTC+10:30. Madrid, Spain in early October is usually on CEST, which is UTC+2.

So Adelaide is 8 hours 30 minutes ahead of Madrid at that date.

10:00 AM on 2026-10-06 in Adelaide minus 8 hours 30 minutes = 01:30 on 2026-10-06 in Madrid.

ANSWER: 2026-10-06 01:30

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close 6:00 PM Sydney time on October 3, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

On **October 3, 2026**, Sydney is on **AEDT (UTC+11)** because daylight saving time starts there that day. Madrid on **October 3, 2026** is still on **CEST (UTC+2)**.

So Madrid is **9 hours behind** Sydney at that moment.

- **6:00 PM Sydney time** on **2026-10-03**
- minus **9 hours**
- = **9:00 AM** in Madrid on **2026-10-03**

ANSWER: 2026-10-03 09:00
